ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a PNP transistor circuit. The emitter is connected to the power supply node labeled V_EE = 10 V; the base is grounded through resistor R_B; the collector is connected to the output node V0, and this node is connected to ground through resistor R_C. The problem gives |V_BE| = 0.7 V, β = 50, R_B = 100 kΩ, and asks for R_C when V0 = 5 V. Reasoning: According to the conduction condition of the PNP transistor, the emitter voltage is +10 V, so the base voltage VB = 10 - 0.7 = 9.3 V. The base resistor is connected from the base to ground, so the base current IB = 9.3 V / 100 kΩ = 93 μA. The collector current IC = βIB = 50 × 93 μA = 4.65 mA. The output node V0 is the collector node, and R_C is connected from this node to ground; it is required that V0 = 5 V, so 5 V = IC R_C. Thus R_C = 5 V / 4.65 mA = 1075 Ω = 1.075 kΩ, approximately 1.07 kΩ.
